name: WSL Process Execution & LOLBIN Abuse
categoryDescription: Modern Windows artifacts — UWP/AppX packages, OneDrive, and Windows Subsystem for Linux.
description: Behavioral abuse of Windows Subsystem for Linux via wsl.exe, wslhost.exe, and bash.exe — used to execute Linux ELF binaries outside Windows-focused EDR visibility, chain LOLBIN commands past process-tree monitoring, or stage a full penetration-testing toolkit (Kali Linux) directly on the host.
forensic_value: Detection here is entirely process/command-line based, not registry-based — this artifact complements the Lxss registry key (which only proves a distro is installed). Key patterns: a Windows LOLBIN (powershell.exe, mshta.exe, rundll32.exe...) spawned as a child of wsl.exe/wslhost.exe; a Windows binary invoked from inside a WSL instance (masquerading the parent/child relationship); bash.exe run with -c or against a script file to indirectly execute commands; or installation/use of the Kali Linux WSL distro, which ships a full offensive toolkit.
